context: A uni student interviews a retired diplomat about postwar history
purpose: Teach: 大都市/過激/騒音/核兵器/虐殺/性別/死ね/無関係

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間をいただきありがとうございます。戦後の大都市圏の復興について、外交官としてのご経験をお聞きしたく参りました。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. I came to ask about your experiences as a diplomat regarding the postwar reconstruction of major metropolitan areas.
lines.style: Formal opening, polite student addressing a senior figure respectfully.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: いやはや、若い方が関心を持ってくださるのは嬉しいことです。当時はね、騒音規制どころか、瓦礫の処理だけで何年もかかった。
lines.en: Well, well, it makes me happy that young people take interest. Back then, forget noise regulations, just clearing the rubble took years.
lines.style: Warm elderly tone, reflective, slightly nostalgic with measured cadence.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。冷戦期には核兵器保有を巡る議論も激しかったと伺いますが、現場ではどう感じておられましたか。
lines.en: I see. I've heard that during the Cold War, debates over nuclear weapons possession were intense — how did it feel on the ground?
lines.style: Probing but respectful, academic curiosity drives the follow-up question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 怖かったですよ。一部の過激派は声を荒げて「死ねばいい」とまで叫んでいた。冷静な交渉が本当に難しい時代でした。
lines.en: It was frightening. Some radicals raised their voices, even shouting things like 'just drop dead.' Calm negotiation was truly difficult back then.
lines.style: Somber, reflective gravity, slight pause conveying weight of memory.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 歴史的虐殺の記憶も、外交の席では避けて通れなかったと思います。性別を問わず多くの市民が犠牲になったわけですから。
lines.en: I imagine memories of historical massacres couldn't be avoided at the diplomatic table. Citizens of every gender suffered, after all.
lines.style: Earnest, thoughtful, weighing words carefully as a respectful student.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: その通り。被害者の声を「自分とは無関係だ」と切り捨てる外交官もいましたが、私はそれだけは許せなかった。
lines.en: Exactly so. Some diplomats dismissed victims' voices as 'unrelated to themselves,' but that was the one thing I could never accept.
lines.style: Firm conviction, slow emphatic delivery, moral clarity in elder's voice.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 胸に刻みます。本日のお話、卒業論文に活かさせていただきます。ありがとうございました。
lines.en: I'll take that to heart. I'll make use of today's discussion in my graduation thesis. Thank you so much.
lines.style: Sincere closing, gratitude tinged with thoughtful resolve and humility.
